rmt-2016-geo-01.prompt: Form a triangle $ABC$ with side lengths $AB=12$, $AC=8$, and $BC=15$. Let the altitude from $A$ to $BC$ intersect $BC$ at $D$ and let $AE$ be the angle bisector of $\angle BAC$, where $E$ is on $BC$. Compute the length of $DE$.

rmt-2016-geo-03.prompt: Compute the area of the largest square that can be inscribed in a unit cube. You may assume that the square's vertices lie on the edges of the cube.

rmt-2016-geo-04.prompt: Inside a circle of radius $1$ are three circles of equal radius such that each of them is tangent to the other two and to the large circle. Determine the radius of one of the smaller circles.

rmt-2016-geo-05.prompt: When circles of the same radius are packed into the plane with maximum density they form a regular lattice. Compute the packing density of this arrangement, that is, the fraction of area covered by circles.

rmt-2016-geo-07.prompt: Consider a circular sector of unit radius and angle $\arcsin\left(\frac13\right)$. Let $S$ be a square inscribed in the sector such that the axis of symmetry of the sector passes through the center of $S$, is parallel to two of the sides of $S$, and all four vertices of $S$ are on the boundary of the sector. What is the area of $S$?

rmt-2016-geo-08.prompt: Natasha walks along a closed convex polygonal curve of length $2016$. She carries a paintbrush of length $1$ and walking all the way around paints all the area as far as she can reach on the outside of the curve. What is that area?
